rationale: The hypothesis posits genotype-phenotype correlations contrasting dominant de novo missense variants with biallelic loss-of-function variants and contrasting Kelch or BTB domain missense variants with truncation variants. The empirical literature establishing KLHL20-related neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #621390; Sleyp et al., 2022) refutes these premises: the disorder is inherited in an autosomal dominant manner caused strictly by de novo missense variants, all of which cluster exclusively in the Kelch-type beta-propeller domain (11/14 possessing the recurrent p.Gly357Arg variant, and 3 possessing other Kelch-domain variants, with 0 variants in the BTB domain). No biallelic loss-of-function or pathogenic truncation variants have been established in human disease cohorts.

evidence.text: All 14 identified individuals with KLHL20-related neurodevelopmental disorder had de novo missense variants clustering exclusively in the Kelch-type beta-propeller domain (11 with recurrent p.Gly357Arg, and 3 other distinct missense variants), presenting with mild to severe intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, and subtle facial dysmorphisms. No biallelic loss-of-function, truncation, or BTB domain variants were described.

source.title: De novo missense variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptor KLHL20 cause a developmental disorder with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder
source.quote: We studied 14 patients with de novo missense variants in KLHL20, delineating a genetic syndrome with patients having mild to severe intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, and subtle dysmorphic facial features. We observed a recurrent de novo missense variant in 11 patients (NM_014458.4:c.1069G>A p.[Gly357Arg]). The recurrent missense and the 3 other missense variants all clustered in the Kelch-type β-propeller domain of the KLHL20 protein, which shapes the substrate binding surface.

conflicts: The hypothesis assumes biallelic loss-of-function and truncation mechanisms exist for KLHL20, but only monoallelic dominant de novo missense variants in the Kelch domain have been documented in affected individuals.
The hypothesis posits missense variants in the BTB domain, whereas all 14 delineated patients harbor missense variants confined strictly to the Kelch-type beta-propeller domain.

new_directions.question_text: Do KLHL20 Kelch-domain missense variants act through dominant-negative sequestration of CUL3-RING substrates or neomorphic gain-of-function degradation?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether the recurrent p.Gly357Arg variant prevents degradation of physiological substrates (such as DAPK or Coronin 7) or stabilizes aberrant complexes will define the cellular mechanism underlying the neurodevelopmental phenotype.

new_directions.question_text: What specific facial and behavioral features reliably differentiate KLHL20 neurodevelopmental disorder from other CUL3-adaptor encephalopathies (e.g., KBTBD8, KLHL7)?
new_directions.rationale: Systematic deep phenotyping using standardized HPO terms across larger international cohorts is required to pinpoint distinguishing clinical discriminators beyond non-specific ASD, hyperactivity, and febrile seizures.
